text: The ___ starts the flow; the ___ must already be true.
explanation: Selecting 'plot data' triggers; being logged in pre-exists. Swapping them is the classic half-mark loss (2022 Q2.2a).

text: An average ___ shall complete a defined ___ within a ___ , with a stated ___ .
explanation: User class + task + time/effort bound + success criterion. 'The system' and 'password' fail the enables-vs-obligates test — rules, not usability.

options: Users must enter a password to log in
An average user shall log in within 30 seconds unaided, 9 of 10 succeeding
The system must count logins per day

distractor.0: That obligates the user — a business rule, not an ability the system enables.
distractor.2: Counting is a function with a writable flow — an FR in disguise.

explanation: Only the middle option enables (not obligates) with user, task, bound and bar. The other two fail scope and category respectively.

prompt: POFOD is the right metric for a continuously displayed vital-signs monitor.

distractor.0: Continuous display has no discrete 'demands' — availability (uptime fraction) fits. POFOD suits on-demand checks like ticket validation.

explanation: False — the classic metric mismatch. Match the metric to the usage pattern or the requirement is nonsense.
